executive_summary: The margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0% through gross margin and e-commerce, not mainly wages – Gross margin and e-commerce caused 79% of the fall; the 3.0% target needs about $30M more a year (p. 5–7)
Dropping money-losing promotions adds up to $10.5M a year and private label $4.1M more – 38% of FY2025 promotion events lost money; deeper promotions have not stopped losses near ValuMart (p. 9–15)
Fix routines where hours are fewest and trim hours only where most: about $7.0M, not an 8% cut – Store labor caused 13% of the fall; a chain-wide cut could lose up to two-thirds to shrink (p. 17–23)

slides.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline
Key questions

claims.claim: Which actions should Harlow take, and in what order, to lift its operating margin from 1.0% in FY2025 to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost?
evidence: Decision maker: CEO, presenting the margin plan to the board for approval

Success criteria: Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028; At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028; Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant); No early closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; Home delivery kept in some form
Timing: Board meeting, February 2027
Out of scope: Exiting home delivery entirely (owners' commitment); New stores and remodels; Refinancing or renegotiating the covenant

Sub-questions: 1 Where did the margin go, and how much must the plan deliver? 2 How much gross margin can promotions and private label win back? 3 Should Harlow cut store hours, and what would it do to shrink? 4 What should Harlow do about home delivery and its weakest stores? 5 Which actions come first, and does the plan meet the board's tests?

slides.title: Where the margin went
Gross margin and e-commerce caused 79% of the margin fall; store labor, the focus of the draft plan, caused far less

claims.claim: 79% of the margin erosion since FY2023, valued at FY2025 sales, came from gross margin and e-commerce
evidence: Operating income bridge, $M: At FY2023 margin 50.7; Gross margin 15.32; E-commerce 12.6; Store labor 4.5; Occupancy 2.98; FY2025 actual 15.3
Operating income fell from $47.9M to $15.3M while sales grew 5.8%

claims.claim: Gross margin: down about one percentage point of sales as promotions deepened and shrink rose
E-commerce: fulfillment cost grew faster than online sales as more orders went to the home
Store labor and occupancy: together about a fifth; wages rose, but hours per sale fell
evidence: Other SG&A held its share of sales and adds nothing

slides.title: Deeper promotions cost the most gross margin, and private label won back only a quarter of it

claims.claim: 69% of the net fall in gross margin came from deeper promotions
evidence: Contribution to change in gross margin, pp of sales: Deeper promotions -0.7; Higher shrink -0.5; More private label 0.18
Gross margin fell from 26.0% to 25.0% of sales

claims.claim: Promotions: promotional sales rose from 24.0% to 29.0% of sales, and each promoted sale earns 14 percentage points less margin
Shrink: up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales, mostly fresh waste and receiving errors
Private label: share up from 17.0% to 18.5%, at 12 percentage points more margin than national brands

Equal to 1.98 percentage points of sales

claims.claim: $4.7M more operating income needed in FY2026 to meet the lender's $20M covenant

claims.claim: $25M the most the plan may spend one-time over FY2026–FY2028

Favors levers that need no capital

claims.claim: The first year has to pay back fast; the structural steps can follow in FY2027–28

Gross margin can recover through fewer money-losing promotions and more private label, not by matching ValuMart

slides.title: 2b: Harlow should compete on fresh produce and convenience, the reasons shoppers give, and spend on price only near ValuMart

slides.title: Where the margin went
Seven actions would lift operating income from $15.3M to $44.9M by FY2028, if promotions deliver in full

claims.claim: Seven actions would lift operating income from $15.3M to $44.9M by FY2028
evidence: Bridge $M: FY2025 15.3; Promotions 10.52; Private label 4.06; Store routines 3.76; Trim Q4 hours 3.26; Delivery fees 2.48; Close six 4.43; Exit three 2.21; Sales base 1.11; FY2028 plan 44.91
$44.9M ÷ $1,411.9M = 3.2% operating margin, against the 3.0% target

claims.claim: Promotions are the largest step and the least certain

slides.title: The draft labor plan would reach only about 1.4% by FY2028, because higher shrink could cancel most of its saving

claims.claim: Only the recommended plan reaches the target
evidence: Draft plan: cuts store hours 8%, freezes e-commerce; gain $5.1M; shrink could rise up to 0.6 pp; $10.4M e-commerce loss stays; no one-time cost; FY2028 margin 1.4% (($15.3M + $5.1M) ÷ $1,503M)
Recommended plan: gain $29.6M; shrink falls about 0.25 pp; e-commerce loss cut by about $2.5M; one-time cost $7.5M; FY2028 margin 3.2% ($44.9M ÷ $1,412M), if promotions deliver

normalized.recommendation: Fix promotions, store routines and delivery fees and close nine weak stores, not cut hours across the board: about 3.2% by FY2028. assumptions_and_uncertainties: The briefing pack has no FY2026 figures; FY2025 is treated as the latest actual year and FY2026 as the first plan year; FY2026 may have closed by February 2027, so test the covenant on actuals
Promotion gain of $10.5M is an upper bound: it assumes shoppers keep buying the items at regular price; lost margin on extra units of dropped events means the real gain is lower
How much traffic the extra promotions saved is not known, which is why the plan tests further cuts store by store
Without the second promotion step the plan reaches about 2.9%, short of 3.0%
Shrink cost of the 8% hours cut is an upper bound: all of the FY2023–25 shrink rise is put down to fewer hours; theft and other causes assumed unchanged
The 12 percentage point private-label margin gap holds as the range widens
Theft, a third of shrink, is not counted on to fall
If some hours must be added in low-staffed stores, part of the shrink gain is spent
Best-staffed quarter's labor taken as a quarter of the $181.9M bill, a cautious base
E-commerce result relies on survey (30% of online spending new) and finance estimate (20 cents contribution per new dollar)
Delivery fee test results (4 stores, 10 weeks) applied to the whole FY2025 order base; all lost online sales counted as lost

Baseline holds FY2025 flat: no further decline, growth or new ValuMart stores; covenant test holds only if FY2025's decline stops
The 2027 minimum wage rise is not in the base; up to $7.3M a year would cut the margin to about 2.7%
